terms.meaning: An address the app recognizes and maps to a screen.
An app that changes screens without a full reload of the browser page.
The small label on a card showing whether the tool is live or coming soon.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports for the tool card
sections.what: Brings in the in-app link tool, the arrow icon and the icon type.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code. These are the tools the card needs.

sections.name: ToolCardProps
sections.title: Inputs the card accepts
sections.what: Lists the values a parent must give the card: name, slug, subtitle, status with only two allowed values, an optional target address, and an icon.
sections.why: Likely reason: restricting status to two values prevents typos from creating an unknown state.
sections.watch_out: A new status value must be added here and in the drawing code, or the card will fall back to the coming-soon look.

sections.name: ToolCard (part 1)
sections.title: Card look and content
sections.what: Builds the inside of the card: an icon tile, a status badge reading Live or Coming soon, the tool name and subtitle, and an Open prompt when the tool is live. Colors and styles change with the live state.
sections.why: Likely reason: visual differences make live and coming-soon tools easy to tell apart at a glance.
sections.watch_out: The test labels are built from the slug, so renaming a slug changes the labels automated tests look for.

sections.name: ToolCard: if
sections.title: Choosing the link type or a dimmed card
sections.what: If the tool is live and has a target, the whole card becomes a clickable link. Outside addresses, pages ending in html, and a few named paths use a plain link that loads a full page. Other targets use the in-app link. Otherwise, draws a dimmed card that does not respond to clicks.
sections.why: The code comment says static pages and outside targets must fully reload, because the in-app link would take them into the app and miss the file.
sections.watch_out: The list of named paths is hardcoded, so a new static tool must be added to it or it will break.

summary: A card on the tools grid showing a tool's name, description and status. Live tools can be clicked; coming-soon tools are dimmed.
purpose: Shows which tools exist and lets users open the live ones.
why: Likely reason: the visual difference between live and coming-soon cards tells users which tools are ready to use.
how: Works out whether the tool is live. Draws the card with an icon, a status badge, the name and the description. If the tool is live and has a target, wraps the card in a link: a plain link for outside addresses and for static pages, or an in-app link for other pages. Otherwise draws a dimmed card that ignores clicks.
inputs: The name, slug, subtitle, status (LIVE or COMING_SOON), an optional target address, and the icon.
outputs: A card on screen, and navigation when a live tool with a target is clicked.
risks: The list of paths that need a full page load is written into the code. A new static tool at a new path would open inside the app and may fail to load. A live tool with no target is drawn dimmed, so it looks coming-soon.
debug: If a card cannot be clicked, check that its status is LIVE and that a target is set. If a tool opens a blank in-app page, add its path to the full page load list. If the badge looks wrong, check the class names in the badge.
